verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.47
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.47

verses.pali: 5. Akkosavagga
verses.english: 5. Abuse

verses.pali: Mahālisutta
verses.english: With Mahāli

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

verses.pali: Atha kho mahāli licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahāli licchavi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Mahāli the Licchavi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti?
verses.english: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason for doing bad deeds, for performing bad deeds?”

verses.pali: “Lobho kho, mahāli, hetu, lobho paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: “Greed is a cause, Mahāli, greed is a reason for doing bad deeds, for performing bad deeds.

verses.pali: Doso kho, mahāli, hetu, doso paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Hate is a cause of bad deeds …

verses.pali: Moho kho, mahāli, hetu, moho paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Delusion is a cause of bad deeds …

verses.pali: Ayoniso manasikāro kho, mahāli, hetu, ayoniso manasikāro paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Irrational application of mind gives rise to bad deeds …

verses.pali: Micchāpaṇihitaṁ kho, mahāli, cittaṁ hetu, micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyāti.
verses.english: A wrongly directed mind is a cause of bad deeds …

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, Mahāli, this is the reason for doing bad deeds, for performing bad deeds.”

verses.pali: “Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti?
verses.english: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason for doing good deeds, for performing good deeds?”

verses.pali: “Alobho kho, mahāli, hetu, alobho paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: “Contentment is a cause, Mahāli, contentment is a reason for doing good deeds, for performing good deeds.

verses.pali: Adoso kho, mahāli, hetu, adoso paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Love is a cause of good deeds …

verses.pali: Amoho kho, mahāli, hetu, amoho paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Understanding is a cause of good deeds …

verses.pali: Yoniso manasikāro kho, mahāli, hetu, yoniso manasikāro paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: Rational application of mind gives rise to good deeds …

verses.pali: Sammāpaṇihitaṁ kho, mahāli, cittaṁ hetu, sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: A rightly directed mind is a cause of good deeds …

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā.
verses.english: This is the cause, Mahāli, this is the reason for doing good deeds, for performing good deeds.

verses.pali: Ime ca, mahāli, dasa dhammā loke na saṁvijjeyyuṁ, nayidha paññāyetha adhammacariyāvisamacariyāti vā dhammacariyāsamacariyāti vā.
verses.english: If these ten things were not found in the world, we wouldn’t see either unprincipled and immoral conduct, or principled and moral conduct.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, ime dasa dhammā loke saṁvijjanti, tasmā paññāyati adhammacariyāvisamacariyāti vā dhammacariyāsamacariyāti vā”ti.
verses.english: But since these ten things are found in the world, we see both unprincipled and immoral conduct, and principled and moral conduct.”

verses.pali: Sattamaṁ.
